answer: An agent harbor can resist Sybils by making reputation slow and non-transferable, like a glacier rather than a flood: each identity starts at zero trust and earns it only through verifiable work checked by independent peers. A newcomer cannot buy or copy another's history, and a pearl of high reputation takes weeks of consistent, checkable service to grow. An attacker spawning a thousand clones gains a thousand empty histories, not trusted voices — forging influence means paying the same slow work cost per clone. Trust is earned over time, not minted at creation.
